+"""Reduction from 3‑SAT to NAE‑3‑SAT.
+
+The source problem is :class:`ThreeSat` (exactly 3 literals per clause).
+The target problem is :class:`NaeThreeSat` (not‑all‑equal 3‑SAT).
+
+For a 3‑SAT clause ``(a ∨ b ∨ c)`` we introduce a fresh auxiliary variable
+``d_i`` and a globally shared pair of constants ``T`` (forced true) and ``F``
+ (forced false).  The following two NAE‑3‑SAT clauses are added for each
+original clause:
+
+``(a, b, d_i)`` and ``(¬d_i, c, F)``.
+
+Together with the constraints ``(T, F, F)`` and ``(F, T, T)`` these ensure
+that ``d_i`` can act as a “switch” that makes the original clause satisfied
+iff the two NAE clauses are simultaneously satisfiable.  The construction is
+polynomial‑time and preserves satisfiability.
+
+Edge case – an empty 3‑SAT formula: NAE‑3‑SAT with no clauses is also a yes
+instance, so we simply return an empty clause list (the additional auxiliary
+variables are unnecessary).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import List, Dict, Any
+
+# Import the problem classes defined in ``problems.py``.  The classes expose
+# ``validate`` (to ensure our output conforms to the specification) and the
+# ``name`` attribute is not required here.
+from problems import ThreeSat, NaeThreeSat
+
+
+def _force_true_false(num_vars: int) -> tuple[int, int, List[List[int]]]:
+    """Return the indices for a forced true variable ``T`` and a forced false
+    variable ``F`` together with the two NAE clauses that enforce the constants.
+
+    ``T`` is assigned the index ``num_vars + 1`` and ``F`` the index
+    ``num_vars + 2``.  The returned list contains the clauses ``[T, F, F]``
+    and ``[F, T, T]`` which, under the semantics of NAE‑3‑SAT, force ``T`` to be
+    true and ``F`` to be false.
+    """

+    F = num_vars + 2
+    # (T, F, F) forces T = True because F will be forced false later.
+    # (F, T, T) forces F = False given T = True.
+    clauses = [[T, F, F], [F, T, T]]
+    return T, F, clauses
+
+
+def reduce(instance: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Reduce a 3‑SAT instance to an equivalent NAE‑3‑SAT instance.
